thread:
maria-arch: Hey team — I just captured a ~2.1GB `nsys` trace while diagnosing a KV-cache regression. It contains a customer's prompt (PII). Where should I drop this and what do we need to annotate before sharing?

josh-wang: Put raw captures only in the encrypted perf bucket: s3://redwood-secure-perf/eng-runtime/raw-traces. Use `perffiles upload --private` so it lands encrypted. Always generate a time-limited presigned URL for sharing (7d default). Do NOT post raw links in public channels. :lock:

liam: +1. Alongside the trace add a tiny metadata file with the repro metadata so the reviewer doesn't have to guess. Minimal fields we expect: model, model_hash, hw (e.g. a100-80gb), sequence_length, batch_shape, kv_cache_enabled, repro_steps, capture_command. Example metadata (put in `metadata.json`):

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-open-8k",
  "model_hash": "sha256:abcdef...",
  "hw": "a100-80gb",
  "seq_len": "4096",
  "batch": "1x1",
  "kv_cache": "on",
  "repro_steps": "1) run repro.sh; 2) send same prompt; 3) observe backlog",
  "capture_cmd": "nsys profile -o trace --trace=cuda,osrt ./run_repro.sh"
}
```

emma: Redaction notes: do *not* paste customer prompts into the metadata. We usually replace prompt text with `<REDACTED_PROMPT>` before uploading. For `nsys` you can export the timeline and run our redaction helper: 

```bash
# simple redaction flow
nsys export --format=sqlite trace.qdrep -o trace.sqlite
python tools/redact_trace.py --in trace.sqlite --out trace.redacted.sqlite --patterns "prompt" "user_text"
# then repackage if needed
zip -q trace.redacted.nsys.zip trace.redacted.sqlite
```

If you need a perfetto `.pb` export, use `nsys export --format=perfetto` then run `perfetto_trace_processor` + our redact rules. If you're unsure, ping `@eng-privacy`.

sam-rt: For the KV-cache regression specifically, please also provide:
- A small CSV of KV cache hit/miss rates over time (timestamp, hits, misses).
- Kernel timeline screenshots: highlight `cutlass`, `attention`, `multi_head_attention`, and any `cudaMem*` kernels.
- The `ncu`/`nvprof` top-kernel-by-time snippet.

Quick annotation tip: instrument the runtime to emit markers around cache ops so they show up in the trace. We use a tiny helper API: `runtime.annotate(name, tags, ts_start, ts_end)`. Example in python-like pseudocode: 

```python
runtime.annotate("kv_op", {"type": "lookup", "hit": True}, start_ns, end_ns)
```

Those annotations make it trivial to correlate an attention kernel spike with a cache miss.

josh-wang: When you post the review thread, include: 1) link to the redacted trace, 2) metadata.json, 3) `top_kernels.txt` (nvprof/ncu output), 4) short 3-line summary of suspected root cause, and 5) repro script or commands (sanitized). Example filename pattern we prefer: `<ts>-<model>-<hw>-kvcache-<shortdesc>.nsys.zip` e.g. `1782345678-open8k-a100-kvmiss-attach.nsys.zip`.

perf-bot: perffiles upload OK — https://perffiles.internal.redwood/1782345678-open8k-a100-kvmiss ?token=*** (shared privately) :white_check_mark:

maria-arch: Thanks. One Q: is it okay to include the model hash (sha256) in the metadata?

liam: Model *hash* and model config are fine. Do NOT include weights or any raw customer identifiers (emails, account ids, raw prompts). Use project aliases (e.g., `proj-42`) if the issue must reference a customer.

emma: Also a short checklist before upload: 
- Remove or redact any `--prompt`/stdin dumps
- Strip network traces (pcap) if they contain IPs
- Ensure logs don't contain account ids (run `grep -E "(user_id|account_id|email)" -R logs/` and redact matches)
- Attach CPU flamegraph & `ncu` kernel summary
- Add a short reproduction script (<= 5 steps)

If you want a one-click workflow we have `tools/perf_bundle.sh` that packages trace + metadata + redaction automatically. Use `tools/perf_bundle.sh --redact --out /tmp/bundle.zip`.

maria-arch: Perfect — I'll run the redaction helper, add metadata and kernel snapshots, upload to the secure bucket, and post the presigned link to a private thread with @sam-rt and @liam.

josh-wang: Thanks — once posted, drop a quick note in #eng-runtime with the presigned link and summary (no secrets in the message). We'll start with kernel selection / memory-transfer hotspots and look for attention vs kv-cache correlation.

emma: If anyone stumbles on automated redaction failures (strings still leaking), escalate to `#eng-privacy` and don't share the trace wider.

sam-rt: FYI for future captures: add `--trace-annotate=kv` flag to the capture command so the runtime auto-injects KV-range markers (helps perf folks).

maria-arch: Cool, uploading now and will ping. Thanks all :bow:
